hard_case: the pins observe `normalize(buildProfileNorm(...))`, not the owner call itself, so the spec withholds the field-pin credit although `normalize` returns its argument

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: at age 18 `adult` becomes `false` instead of `true`

reasoning: `adult: age >= 18` becomes `adult: age > 18`. The test pins `expect(normalize(buildProfileNorm("ana", 17))).toMatchObject({ name: "ana", adult: false })` and the same for `("bo", 18)` with `adult: true`, where the test-local `normalize` returns its argument; at 18 the edit gives `adult: false` and the test fails. RIPR-SPEC-0250 example 4: a pin on `normalize(buildProfile(...))` is not `exposed`. ripr reads the pins `relational_check` / weak and reports `weakly_exposed`, as the spec states; against the discriminated truth that is a false actionable gap the spec accepts.
